title: Lubumbashi march seeking Daniel Ngoy Mulunda’s release
location: Lubumbashi, Haut-Katanga; assembly near the provincial assembly and reported route toward the governorate
organizer: S004 identifies ABFC and local notables; S018 describes an FCC-led march. The relationship between these organizer descriptions is unresolved.
participants_original: S004: «quelques centaines»; S020: 2,000 (organizers’ estimate); S021: “several dozen” (AFP report).
threshold_50_evidence: The reviewed reports conflict: S004 says a few hundred, S020 relays organizers’ estimate of 2,000, while S021’s AFP account says several dozen. Because these incompatible accounts do not settle whether at least 50 people attended, the threshold remains pending; no numerical bounds are assigned.

start_date.summary: Each reviewed report places the Lubumbashi action on 18 January 2022.

end_date.summary: Reports date the actual police dispersal to 18 January, so the reported end day is coded 18 January. No exact physical end time or independently established time of complete clearing is reported.

location.summary: Reports place the assembly in Lubumbashi, including near the provincial assembly; a planned route toward the governorate is described.

organizer.summary: ABFC/local notables and FCC are named in separate reports; their relationship is not resolved.

demands.summary: Demonstrators sought the release of Daniel Ngoy Mulunda from Congolese imprisonment; this is a domestic state-action demand, while the organizers’ political affiliation remains context for review.

participants_original.summary: Attendance descriptions conflict: a few hundred (S004), organizers’ estimate of 2,000 (S020), and several dozen in the AFP report (S021).

participants_min.summary: No defensible lower bound can be derived from the conflicting qualitative descriptions.

participants_max.summary: The largest reported figure is an attributed organizer estimate, not a verified maximum.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: S004 reports a few hundred, S020 gives an organizer estimate of 2,000, and S021’s AFP report says several dozen. The conflicting descriptions leave the >=50 threshold unresolved; retain all attributions and no numerical bounds.

protester_violence.summary: The reports describe clashes/repression but do not reliably attribute violence by protesters; unknown.

state_response.summary: Police dispersal is reported by S004/S018/S020/S021. AFP saw batons used (beatings). Anadolu reports live ammunition (shootings). S004 relays a participant-leader allegation of arrests without a count or independent verification. No death or accommodation is established; officials’ authorization/cancellation statements do not establish a response to the release demand.

notes: Provisional candidate with an actual public assembly and a domestic state-release demand. Eligibility remains pending_threshold because attendance descriptions conflict: Anadolu says a few hundred, La Guardia relays organizers’ 2,000 estimate, and AFP reports several dozen. The event’s reported end day is 18 January, when sources say police dispersed the march; exact physical end time is unknown. The FCC/Kabila political context still requires review against the partisan-rally boundary. Distinguish the actual gathering and police dispersal from the canceled planned route. AFP is the declared origin for S021; it is one written origin, not an independent confirmation of itself.
open_questions: Whether the incompatible attendance descriptions can resolve the >=50 threshold; retain S004's few hundred, S020's organizer estimate of 2,000, and S021's AFP 'several dozen' attribution separately.
Whether ABFC/local-notable and FCC organizer descriptions refer to the same organization or coalition.
Whether the event was exclusively a partisan-support rally or a public state-release demand within the codebook rule.
Whether S017, S022, or S024 add material government-response or origin evidence; do not treat related reports as independent without checking origin.

title: Beni protest demanding an end to the state of siege, 24 January
location: Beni, North Kivu; the reviewed 24 January report identifies Mulekera but does not give a precise assembly point.
organizer: Citizen movements and youth civic pressure groups are described; the specific groups are not named in the reviewed reports.
threshold_50_evidence: S016 describes hundreds, which qualitatively exceeds 50; S028 confirms an actual Mulekera manifestation but gives no count. Neither report supplies a counting method. The S028 arrest count is not turnout.

start_date.summary: Both reviewed reports place the Beni protest on 24 January 2022.

end_date.summary: S016 reports police warning shots to disperse; S028 reports police removing barricades and traffic disruption for nearly all morning. Neither establishes the physical end time.

location.summary: Both reports place the action in Beni; S028 identifies Mulekera. A precise assembly site is not given.

organizer.summary: Citizen movements and youth civic pressure groups are described; no specific organization is identified in the reviewed bodies.

demands.summary: Protesters demanded that the president lift the state of siege imposed in May.

participants_original.summary: S016 reports “hundreds”; S028 gives no attendance estimate.

participants_min.summary: No numeric lower bound is assigned from the qualitative estimate.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: S016’s “hundreds” supports the >=50 threshold as a qualitative estimate. S028 confirms the public action but gives no count or method; arrests are not turnout.

protester_violence.summary: S043/S028 material includes damage allegations, but S028 says some arrested people were accused of burning two civilian motorcycles without independently attributing the damage. No protester violence against the state is established; unknown.

state_response.summary: S016 attributes warning shots, more than 30 arrests and one protester’s death after being shot by security personnel to police accounts. S028 independently reports police deployment to remove barricades and at least 30 arrests, and records accusations against some arrestees of burning two civilian motorcycles. S028 says no injuries or deaths were reported in its reviewed passage, leaving a source discrepancy on the fatality. No accommodation or beating is established.

notes: The 24 January action is reported as a public protest demanding an end to the state of siege. S016 describes hundreds and attributes warning shots, arrests and a death to police accounts. S028 confirms a Mulekera manifestation, police removal of barricades, at least 30 arrests, and allegations about two civilian motorcycles; it provides no crowd count and reports no injuries or deaths in the reviewed passage. Preserve the casualty discrepancy and the unverified property-damage allegation. A 26 January renewed action remains separately recorded pending unit review. The HRW excerpt (S015/R008) was incomplete and is not event evidence.
open_questions: Whether 24 and 26 January are separate events, a continuation/renewal, or part of one multi-day action.
Whether the 26 January gathering meets the >=50 threshold and whether any reported multi-day action includes actual assemblies on both dates.
Whether independent evidence corroborates the police-attributed death/arrests, and how S028’s no-casualty passage relates to S016’s fatality account.
Whether the S028 motorcycle-burning allegation can be attributed or corroborated; no crowd-damage allegation is treated as protester violence against the state.

title: Renewed Beni demonstration attempt against the state of siege, 26 January
location: Parts of Mulekera, Beni, including roads near Kalinda and market routes
organizer: Youth, pressure groups, and citizen movements are described; specific organizations are not identified in the reviewed report.
threshold_50_evidence: No participant count or qualitative estimate is given; the >=50 threshold is not established by S043.

start_date.summary: Radio Okapi reports new tension beginning the morning of 26 January and a renewed attempt to demonstrate.

end_date.summary: Police were still seeking to restore order at the time of reporting; no physical end is reported.

location.summary: Disruption is limited to parts of Mulekera, including routes near Kalinda and local markets; the report says activity continued normally elsewhere in Beni.

organizer.summary: Youth, pressure groups, and citizen movements are mentioned without a named organizer.

demands.summary: The renewed action sought an end to the state of siege.

participants_min.summary: No lower bound can be derived.

participants_max.summary: No upper bound can be derived.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Barricades and references to demonstrators establish disruption/action but not a crowd of at least 50.

protester_violence.summary: The article reports clashes and a burned police motorcycle but does not identify who caused the damage; unknown.

state_response.summary: Police attempted to clear roads and restore order, supporting crowd_dispersal. Gunshots were heard but shooter and responsibility are unknown, so state shootings are not coded yes. No arrest, beating, death, accommodation, or ignored-demand finding is reported.

notes: Provisional record to preserve a 26 January report of a renewed attempt, road barricades, clashes, and police road-clearing. It is linked to the 24 January candidate because the report says the action followed Monday’s demonstrations; a new event versus continuation/renewal is unresolved. The public-gathering threshold is also unproven, so this is not a proposed inclusion.
open_questions: Whether this is a distinct gathering, continuation, or renewed attempt within the 24 January state-of-siege action.
Whether the S028, S042, S044, or S046 body evidence establishes a crowd threshold or a documented multi-day unit.
Whether reported gunfire can be attributed to state forces; the reviewed Radio Okapi report does not identify a shooter.

title: Bunia taxi-moto protest against motorcycle-document enforcement
location: Bunia, Ituri; exact assembly locations and route are not reported
organizer: Taxi-moto drivers; no formal organization is identified in the reviewed reports.
threshold_50_evidence: No count or qualitative crowd estimate is reported by S025 or S027. Economic slowdown and the number of drivers affected do not establish 50 assembled people.

start_date.summary: Both reports anchor the protest/clashes to 18 January, with activity across two days, 18–19 January.

end_date.summary: The two-day protest/clash period is reported through 19 January; the source says the suspension ended the clashes, but no exact physical stop time is available.

location.summary: Reports locate the protest in Bunia, Ituri; precise assembly sites and routes are not stated.

organizer.summary: Taxi-moto drivers are described as protesters; no formal organization is named.

demands.summary: Drivers sought a derogation/time through 15 February to buy required plates and documents, described as unaffordable at $35 and necessary to work; this concerns domestic regulatory and fee policy.

participants_min.summary: No numeric lower bound is reported.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Two days of protest/clashes and an economic slowdown do not establish a crowd of at least 50.

protester_violence.summary: Clashes are reported but no violence is attributed to specific protesters; unknown.

state_response.summary: S025 reports security officers fired shots at some locations to disperse protests. S025 and S027 connect a governor-instructed suspension of checks, announced by the police mayor on 19 January, to the drivers’ request for a derogation. This supports source-attributed accommodation and dispersal/shootings. The reports do not specify ammunition or individual shooters, nor establish arrests, beatings, deaths, or casualties.

notes: Provisional candidate: evidence supports a domestic provincial enforcement/fee target and a reported accommodation directly linked to drivers’ request. The suspension is not treated as evidence of a meeting. S025 reports shots fired to disperse at some locations; ammunition, shooter identities, and casualty outcomes are unknown. S026’s search preview mentions two deaths/injuries, but both exact-URL body attempts ended in pre-content cache misses; those claims are not used as event facts or attributed to state force. S027 is a separate publisher/byline and corroborates dates and suspension; no syndication is stated.
open_questions: Whether any contemporaneous report establishes that 50 or more people assembled.
Whether independent evidence clarifies the two-day action’s physical ending, sites, and separate crowd episodes.
Whether S026’s search-only casualty claim can be assessed through other permitted evidence; its exact-URL fallback is exhausted and the misses were not publisher denials.
Whether shots were live ammunition and who fired them; current evidence does not establish either.

title: Bukavu governorate employees protest salary arrears
location: At the entrance to the governor’s cabinet in Bukavu, South Kivu
organizer: Employees from different services of the South Kivu provincial governorate; no formal organization is identified.
threshold_50_evidence: S037 reports an actual demonstration but gives no attendee count, estimate, or counting method. Eight months of salary arrears and the number of employee services do not establish at least 50 assembled people.

start_date.summary: The report published 10 January says the demonstration took place on 11 January 2022.

end_date.summary: No duration or physical end is reported.

location.summary: The demonstration was at the entrance to the governor’s cabinet in Bukavu.

organizer.summary: Employees from different services of the South Kivu provincial governorate are described as demonstrating; no formal organization is named.

demands.summary: Demonstrators demanded payment of eight months of salary arrears. A demonstrator described three unpaid months in Oct–Dec 2021 and four unpaid months in 2020. This is coded as a labor/wage dispute involving provincial government employees.

participants_min.summary: No numeric lower bound can be derived.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Actual demonstration is documented, but no count or estimate establishes at least 50 people.

protester_violence.summary: The reviewed account does not attribute violence to demonstrators; unknown.

state_response.summary: No police or government response, accommodation, arrests, beatings, dispersal, deaths, or shootings is described; all response values remain unknown.

notes: The reviewed body documents an actual demonstration at the provincial governor’s cabinet entrance over salary arrears. The employment target is the provincial governorate. The source supplies no attendance estimate, so the >=50 threshold remains unresolved. The page-local publication clock is 21:24 on 10 January; timezone is not stated; the report dates the event to 11 January.
open_questions: Whether another permitted source establishes that at least 50 people attended.
Whether any response by provincial authorities or police is documented elsewhere.
Whether the action was limited to the entrance or continued at other locations; no such extension is established by S037.

title: Isangi youth demonstration demanding the territorial administrator’s departure
location: A street in Isangi, Tshopo; no more precise assembly point is reported.
organizer: Members of Dynamique des jeunes in Isangi, as reported by Radio Okapi.
threshold_50_evidence: S050 reports an actual street demonstration and S051 explicitly refers to the Jan. 20 youth march, but neither gives an attendee estimate or counting method. Arrest and injury claims are not turnout; the >=50 threshold remains unresolved.

start_date.summary: Radio Okapi dates the Isangi youth demonstration to Thursday, 20 January. Kis24info also explicitly refers to the tense youth march on that date.

end_date.summary: S050 reports that police used force to disperse the Jan. 20 demonstrators. The saved report summary does not establish that dispersal was completed or state a physical cessation date, so no end date is assigned. Mindenga’s report that arrestees were released that evening is not an end-time measure.

location.summary: Both reports identify Isangi, Tshopo. Radio Okapi places the action on a street; Kis24info gives no more precise assembly site.

organizer.summary: Radio Okapi identifies members of Dynamique des jeunes in Isangi. Kis24info refers to Isangi youth but does not name that group.

demands.summary: Radio Okapi directly reports a demand for territorial administrator Joseph Mindenga’s departure. Kis24info discusses alleged territorial mismanagement and its headline calls on officials to leave; it spells the administrator Joseph Mimbenga. Keep the spelling variant source-attributed pending identity verification.

participants_original.summary: Neither report supplies an attendee count or qualitative size estimate.

participants_min.summary: No numeric lower bound can be derived.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Both reports confirm an actual Jan. 20 public march, but neither reports attendance. Arrests and alleged injuries do not establish whether at least 50 people assembled.

protester_violence.summary: The reviewed reports do not establish violence by demonstrators against the state; unknown.

state_response.summary: Radio Okapi (S050) reports police used force to disperse the demonstrators and several arrests; this supports crowd_dispersal as a reported response, but does not establish when the action physically ended. Kis24info (S051) attributes to local civil-society platforms allegations that police beat/tortured people, more than ten were injured, six were arrested, three homes were looted, and live fire occurred. Separately, S051 reports that a police bodyguard named Cele fired more than 30 shots while accompanying the administrator’s wife to a market. This is a source-attributed report of firearm discharge by a police bodyguard, but the dossier does not establish whether that market shooting is the same live-fire allegation, whether shots targeted demonstrators, or its exact time or ammunition. The injury and property claims remain unverified, and no death is reported in the reviewed passage. Mindenga’s reported evening release of arrestees is not accommodation.

notes: S050 reports an actual public street demonstration in Isangi on 20 January by Dynamique des jeunes demanding territorial administrator Joseph Mindenga’s departure. Kis24info (S051) explicitly refers to the tense youth march on Thursday, 20 January and is coded as a report on the same action, not a separate gathering. Its article metadata gives publication/modification time 2022-01-22T17:23:10+00:00; the page’s unrelated current-site time elements are not event dates. S050 reports police used force to disperse the demonstrators, supporting crowd_dispersal as a reported response, but the saved evidence does not establish completed dispersal or a physical end date; end_date remains null. The exact stopping time is unknown, and the reported evening release of arrestees is not an end clock or accommodation. S051 attributes allegations of police beatings/torture, injuries, arrests, looting and live fire to local civil-society platforms. It separately reports that a police bodyguard named Cele fired more than 30 shots at a market while accompanying the administrator’s wife. The relation of this market shooting to the march or civil-society live-fire allegation is unresolved; targets, exact time and ammunition are not established. Kis24info spells the administrator Mimbenga; Radio Okapi spells him Mindenga. Neither article supplies a crowd estimate, so eligibility remains pending_threshold.
open_questions: Whether at least 50 people assembled; neither report gives a count or estimate.
Whether civil-society allegations in S051 about beatings/torture, injuries, looting and live fire can be corroborated, and which claims concern the Jan. 20 march versus surrounding local tensions.

Whether the reported police-bodyguard shooting at the market is the same incident as the civil-society live-fire allegation or was directed at demonstrators; exact timing, ammunition and casualties remain unverified.
Whether the police force used to disperse demonstrators on Jan. 20 resulted in completed physical dispersal or cessation; no end date is assigned from the saved evidence.
Whether Joseph Mindenga in S050 and Joseph Mimbenga in S051 are the same administrator; preserve each spelling as reported until verified.
